depth: The depth map shows an indoor checkout counter layout where a red shopping basket (~3–5 m away, bottom left) and the camera wearer's hand holding a green bottle in frame 5 (~3–5 m away) are the brightest, farthest elements, out of the camera wearer's immediate arm's reach. Much nearer in front (~0.3–1.5 m) are the checkout register on the lower right, a standing brown paper bag on the counter, and a person in a blue polo shirt standing behind the counter (~3–5 m away, ~3–5 m from the bag), while a doorway frame on the left (~3–5 m) separates the background from a second person in a plaid shirt (~0.3–1.5 m away on the near right of frame 2, ~0.5 m right of the counter) and nearby store shelving (<1.5 m, dark foreground). Across the 5 frames, the person in blue stays at roughly ~3–5 m but turns his torso from angled away from the back-right register (frames 1–2) to profile facing the bag on his left (frames 3–4) before facing away from the camera wearer in frame 5 as the camera wearer's left hand and bottle enter from the bottom left. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the background doorframe, counter, and paper bag from the shallow store foreground through the open doorway, and confirms the raised package in frame 3 is at roughly the same depth plane as the bag opening. However, the map is unreliable along the open mesh of the red basket—which it fills as a solid bright slab—and it flattens internal facial details and glass panes into uniform grey regions.
segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete background and foreground instances against a black void, consistently detecting the person in the blue shirt (~3–5 m away, left of center, waist-up behind the counter) and a small bottle on the counter (~3–5 m away, lower right, ~3–5 m right of the person) across all 5 frames. In frame 2, it captures the second person in the plaid shirt (~0.3–1.5 m away, facing toward the camera from the near aisle on the right and partly cut off by the right frame edge), and in frame 5 it segments the green bottle held out of reach at ~3–5 m in the camera wearer's bottom-left background alongside a tiny blue 'person' fragment at the lower-right edge (from frame 4's left edge). Across frames 1 to 5, the primary person's mask shows his silhouette rotating from facing back-right while holding a box (which leaves a black unsegmented hole inside his chest mask in frame 1) to facing right in profile with arms extended toward the unsegmented paper bag (frames 3–4), and finally facing away from the camera wearer in frame 5 while his right hand and the wearer's hand overlap the green bottle. While segmentation makes the tiny bottle by the register and the nearby right-edge person stand out more sharply than in the cluttered RGB view, it is highly unreliable for scene layout and objects: it completely omits the counter, walls, brown paper bag, and handheld package, and mislabels the distant red shopping basket (~3–5 m above the person) as a 'chair' in frames 3–5 and nearby shelves (<1.5 m away on the right) as 'book' and 'banana' in frames 1–2.
pose: The pose map renders 2D body (yellow) and hand (magenta) skeletons only for the person in the blue shirt (~3–5 m away from the camera wearer), omitting all foreground structures, objects, the nearby person in frame 2, and the camera wearer's own arm in frame 5. The facial keypoint clusters above the shoulder line track his head orientation across time: angled downward and to the camera's right away from the register and handheld box in frames 1–2, turned into a right-facing profile looking at the paper bag area in frames 3–4 as his torso rectangle narrows almost to a vertical line, and oriented straight away from the camera wearer in frame 5. His arm and hand keypoints trace what is out of his ~3–5 m reach: in frames 1–2, his left arm extends down-right to the register while his right elbow bends to hold the box at chest height; in frame 3, both wrists lift upward to the right above the bag opening; in frame 4, his right arm reaches down-right onto the counter; and in frame 5, his left hand rests near the counter while his right wrist extends down-left to roughly ~3–5 m from the camera wearer's bottle. This skeleton view makes his 3D torso rotation, shoulder-width collapse in profile (frames 3–4), and occluded back-arm trajectory much easier to read than in RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable below the waist (clipped by the counter occlusion), misses the nearby person in frame 2 and the camera wearer's hand in frame 5, and fails to detect magenta finger keypoints whenever the hands move rapidly or are partially occluded in frames 3, 4, and the right hand of frame 5.
